notes: The wiring diagram image was not available, so connections follow the text: OLED and DHT powered from 3.3V, OLED on I2C (SDA/SCL), DHT data on D4. Breadboard hole positions and wire routing are assumed, not read from the diagram.
The tutorial says DHT11, which is not in the catalogue, so a new dht11 type was created with DATA/VCC/GND ports. Its pin order on the module is assumed.

The catalogue nano-matter type lists only D4, 3V3, GND.1 and USB. The I2C pins SDA and SCL are used as ports anyway because the tutorial needs them. The catalogue oled-ssd1306 has no listed ports, so GND, VCC, SCL and SDA are used.
In the thumbnail photo the Nano Matter sits on the breadboard. It is modelled here as wired to the breadboard with jumpers, since the tutorial says to use jumper wires.
The Google Nest Hub Max (Thread border router), the phone app and the computer are not part of the wired circuit, so they are omitted. The USB-C cable's far end is not modelled.
